chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-ʿAbdī, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “If a man were brought to me who had falsely accused a Muslim slave of zinā, and we know of him nothing but good, I would administer to him the prescribed punishment of the free person, minus one lash.”

key_terms.بِالزِّنَى: with the charge of illicit sexual intercourse
key_terms.حَدَّ الْحُرِّ: the punishment assigned in the case of a free person
key_terms.سَوْطًا: a lash or stroke of the whip

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd punishment for falsely accusing a Muslim slave of zinā in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning false accusation of zinā against a Muslim slave known only for goodness. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that the accuser is punished with the hadd of slander nearly equal to that for accusing a free person, reduced by one lash.
